angularDiameterSource: Uniform-disc fit to the 909 squared visibilities of the pinned September 2014 VLTI/PIONIER H-band file (1.62-1.73 um), this package; a uniform disc fits these data poorly (reduced chi-squared 51), which is the granulation the image shows. Paladini et al. (2018, Nature 553, 310) adopt a similar diameter for the same data.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.186 +/- 0.447 mas (Gaia Collaboration 2020, yCat I/350, via SIMBAD), RUWE 2.9; Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) gives 6.13 +/- 0.76 mas, the 163 pc Paladini et al. (2018) use.
radiusSource: The fitted angular diameter at the Gaia distance: 18.17 mas at 161.7 pc is 219,710,723 km, 316 solar radii at 695700 km. Mayer et al. (2014, A&A 570, A113) list 370 solar radii from the bolometric luminosity.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 3200 K from Paladini et al. 2018 (Nature 553, 310; https://doi.org/10.1038/nature25001), Methods, Stellar parameters: the best-fitting S-type MARCS model to the photometry, on a 2000-3200 K grid in 200 K steps. No uncertainty is stated, and 3200 K is the top of the grid.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the fitted radius. The photosphere of an asymptotic giant branch star is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp; the sphere is the reference surface the interferometric image is cast onto, not a measured shape.
